kaikki_vikisozluk.e: مَازَرْيُون or مَازَرِيُون • (māzaryūn or māzariyūn) m
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: From Classical Persian مازریون (māzaryūn), whence also Turkish mezeryon, from ماز (māz, “oak gall”) + زریون (zaryūn, “green, fresh”, literally “gold-coloured”), a dvandva after the berries and leaves of the plant. The Persian is probably borrowed from another Iranian language because the second part of the compound is of restricted, literary use.
